text:
eric-sales: Quick q — Acme insists on buying via AWS Marketplace (their procurement policy) but they want a 12mo committed capacity with a 30% commit discount + net30 invoicing. Can we reflect commit discounts on marketplace invoices or do we need to route off-marketplace? Also they want a 2-week Dedicated POC.

jess-revops: Short answer: marketplace invoices are issued by AWS and won’t automatically show our internal commit discounts. Two patterns we use: 
1) Direct contract: customer signs MSA/commit with us, reserved capacity, we invoice net30.
2) Marketplace purchase at list price + post-sale commercial credit or rebate to reflect the commit. That needs deal-desk & finance to approve and is operationally heavier.

samir-se: For the POC we can spin a Dedicated eval in a sandbox org and tag it as acme-poc. We can mirror commit pricing for evaluation but it’s a manual config. Command I use to create an eval env: ```rdwctl create-poc --profile acme --sku dedicated-eval --term 14d```

mel-procurement: Procurement is rigid: they require AWS Marketplace invoicing only, PO# on invoice, and they'll only accept 45-day payment terms. They explicitly said no manual credits applied after-the-fact. Any flexibility on our side?

dani-legal: Marketplace contracts are governed by AWS terms — that limits our ability to negotiate custom legal terms (indemnities, payment mechanics). If we go direct we need legal to approve exceptions on payment terms and any non-standard termination language.

jess-revops: If procurement won’t budge, hybrid is an option: customer buys a 1yr SKU via marketplace at list price so procurement is happy. We run a shadow commit off-marketplace and apply an annual rebate (contra-revenue) or issue a credit note. Need explicit deal-desk + finance signoff. This preserves procurement flow while giving them committed economics.

eric-sales: Would doing the rebate route impact revenue recognition or make billing reconciliation harder?

jess-revops: It will change invoicing flow — finance treats rebates as contra-revenue usually. We'll need to document the rebate mechanics in the SOW so accounting can map it. I'll loop in @dana-finance.

samir-se: One more technical caveat: marketplace-triggered purchases don’t automatically provision Dedicated endpoints. We need the customer to complete AWS marketplace registration/registration token so we can map their account id; provisioning may be manual and add ~2-3 business days.

procurement-bot: Reminder: please attach customer PO and W-9 to the deal ticket. AWS Marketplace registration required before we can release any customer contact info.

jess-revops: :thumbsup: I'll open a deal-desk ticket. What I need from you, Eric: proposed rate card (list + commit), commit term, customer PO constraints, and any legal exceptions requested.

eric-sales: PO# 123456789. Procurement contact: sara.j@acme.com. They also want a single consolidated invoice for all AWS purchases. I'll DM contact details.

dani-legal: If we do a hybrid rebate, legal needs explicit SOW language describing rebate calculation, timing, and clawback on early termination.

jess-revops: Noted. Opening ticket now: DD-2026-0047. Assigning to @revops and @finance. ETA for decision ~48 hours.

samir-se: I'll prep the POC infra checklist and estimate 2-3 business days to spin up after AWS registration is complete.

eric-sales: Thanks team. Can we sync with Acme procurement on a short call tomorrow 10am PT? I'll send the invite.
